title: Göbekli Tepe as an astronomical calendar tracking the Great Year

tellings.quote: because look at the pillars of quec Tepe have they're just basically star constellations

plain: Göbekli Tepe is a very old site in Turkey with huge carved stone pillars. On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher called Matt says the carvings on those pillars are basically star constellations, so the site worked as a calendar tracking the Great Year, the slow cycle of about 26,000 years in which the stars seem to shift across the sky. If so, the people who built it watched the sky far more closely than is usually thought.
